title: Quasi-identifier in GPS coordinates
description: Live GPS coordinates transmitted by the child's device can serve as quasi-identifiers that, when combined with other data, can uniquely identify the child's identity and movements.

title: Revealing location attributes
description: GPS coordinates are revealing attributes that directly support identification of the data subject's physical location and movement patterns.

title: Small anonymity set for location data
description: In residential or specific areas, GPS coordinates may allow singling out an individual due to the small anonymity set, especially when combined with temporal data.

title: Quasi-identifier linking through GPS data
description: GPS coordinates can be combined with other data (e.g., time, device ID) to link and identify the child through quasi-identifier analysis.

title: Profiling through location patterns
description: Continuous GPS data can be analyzed to profile the child's movement patterns, habits, and routines, enabling inference of personal information.

title: Sensitive location data collection
description: Live GPS coordinates are highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is functionally required for the app's stated purpose.

title: Excessive granularity in location data
description: Live GPS coordinates provide fine-grained location data that may be more detailed than necessary for the functional requirements of the system.

title: Excessive frequency of data collection
description: Transmission of GPS coordinates at regular intervals may occur more frequently than functionally needed, increasing privacy risk.

title: Unawareness of continuous tracking
description: The child (data subject) may not be fully aware of the extent and implications of continuous GPS tracking and data transmission to the backend.

title: Lack of control over data collection preferences
description: The child may lack meaningful control to set preferences or consent regarding how, when, and for how long GPS data is collected and processed.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Continuous collection of live GPS coordinates may process more personal data than is actually needed, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.

title: Unique identifier in geofencing notifications
description: Geofencing notifications may contain unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user ID) that can be used to link data to specific individuals across systems.

title: Quasi-identifier through location and timing data
description: Combination of location data (zone entry/exit) and timestamp can serve as quasi-identifiers that uniquely identify individuals when combined with other data sources.

title: Identifier in geofencing data
description: The notification may contain unique references to the identity of the data subject (child) that enable direct identification.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location and timing data can reveal attributes about the data subject's routine, habits, and movements that support identification.

title: Sensitive location data collection
description: Location data is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is functionally required for simple geofencing notifications.

title: Data propagation to external entity
description: Geofencing data is propagated to the parent (ExternalEntity) where it may be accessible by parties beyond the functional necessity.

title: Unawareness of location tracking
description: Data subjects (children) may not be aware that their location is being tracked and notifications are being generated and sent.

title: Lack of control over data processing
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location data is processed and shared.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing location data may exceed what is actually needed for the geofencing functionality, violating data minimization requirements.

title: Linking through unique identifier in location data
description: Child's location data can be linked to the specific child through unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user account), enabling tracking of the child's movements across contexts.

title: Quasi-identifier combining location with other attributes
description: Location data combined with other attributes (time, location type, family relationships) can serve as quasi-identifiers to uniquely identify the child.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The Mobile App Backend processes identified location data of the child, which is personal data that directly identifies the child's whereabouts.

title: Sensitive location data shared
description: Live location data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be shared when strictly required. Sharing real-time location with a secondary guardian may exceed functional necessity.

title: Excessive location granularity
description: Live location data is disclosed at a very fine-grained level (real-time coordinates), which may be more detailed than functionally needed for guardian access.

title: Data propagation to external party
description: Location data is propagated to an external entity (Secondary Guardian) where it may not be strictly needed, increasing exposure risk.

title: Predetermined party data sharing
description: Location data is shared with a predetermined set of parties (secondary guardian), which is known at design time but still represents data exposure to external entities.

title: Child unawareness of location sharing
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, violating transparency requirements.

title: Lack of child control over location sharing
description: The child may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding who can access their live location data.

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: Sharing live location data may process more personal data than actually needed, potentially violating GDPR data minimization principle.

title: Potential invalid consent for location sharing
description: Consent for sharing child's live location with secondary guardian may not be valid if not properly obtained, informed, or age-appropriate.

title: Location data linked to child identity
description: Live location data can be linked to a specific child through identifiers, enabling tracking and association with the data subject.

title: Location as revealing attribute
description: Live location is a revealing attribute that supports identification of the data subject and can be used to single out the child.
